name: Battle of Poitiers (1356)
note: The accounts do not give compass directions, so the plan has the French at the top and the English at the bottom. The hedge, the marsh and the River Miosson are placed by judgement: the accounts say the marsh lay by Warwick's archers on the English left and the hedge before Salisbury's men on the right, but not exactly where. The French rear divisions stood behind the leading one; their sideways positions are not given. The Captal de Buch's route round the flank, and the side it took, are not given either. Warwick's and Salisbury's divisions are each drawn as one block with their archers.

terrain.quote: a wooded hill in the Fôret de Nouaillé

terrain.name: Marsh
terrain.quote: the archers in Warwick's division were positioned in the edge of a marsh

units.quote: The one on the left was commanded by Thomas, Earl of Warwick, marshal of England

units.name: Salisbury's right division
units.quote: The right flank was under William, Earl of Salisbury

units.name: The Prince's centre division
units.quote: The Black Prince took command of the centre division

units.name: Warwick's pursuers
units.quote: a number, possibly a large number, of men from Warwick's division left their positions and pursued the French

units.name: Captal de Buch's small force
units.quote: send a small mounted group under the Gascon lord Jean, the Captal de Buch, on a circuitous march around the French flank

units.name: Audrehem's mounted knights
units.quote: Audrehem's cavalry attacked Warwick's division on the English left

units.name: Clermont's mounted knights
units.quote: while Clermont charged Salisbury's on the right

units.name: French first division
units.quote: The foremost division was led by the constable of France, Walter, Count of Brienne.

units.name: French second division
units.quote: Behind this was a division led jointly by John's 19-year-old son and heir and John's uncle

units.name: French third division
units.quote: The third division was led by John's younger brother, Philip, Duke of Orléans

units.name: Orléans's departing half
units.quote: marched away from the battle with half of them

units.name: French king's division
units.quote: The rearmost division, of 2,000 men-at-arms and an uncertain number of crossbowmen, was commanded by the king himself.

phases.title: The two armies take their ground
phases.text: The Anglo-Gascons held a wooded hill, the Prince's division behind the other two as a reserve. The French drew up in four divisions, the first about 500 yards from the English.
phases.quote: Initially the Prince's force was held back behind the other two divisions as a reserve.

phases.title: The French cavalry charge the two wings
phases.text: Audrehem's horsemen rode at Warwick's division and Clermont's at Salisbury's. On the left the marsh kept them from the archers. On the right they reached the gap in the hedge and a fierce melee began.
phases.quote: Audrehem's cavalry attacked Warwick's division on the English left, while Clermont charged Salisbury's on the right.

phases.title: The French cavalry and the first division are driven back
phases.text: The French cavalry took heavy casualties and withdrew; Audrehem was captured and Clermont killed. The longbowmen then forced the first division back as well, and its leader, Brienne, the constable of France, was killed.
phases.quote: The French cavalry took heavy casualties and withdrew

phases.title: The second division attacks at the hedge
phases.text: With no pursuit of the survivors, the English held their positions and reformed. The second French division, 4,000 strong, forced its way through the hedge and fought hand to hand for two hours, and the Prince committed almost all of his reserves.

phases.title: The Dauphin's division withdraws
phases.text: Bourbon was killed and the Dauphin's standard-bearer captured, and the Dauphin's advisers took him and two brothers from the front line. The exhausted rest of the division withdrew as well, and the disengagement was orderly.
phases.quote: There was no panic and the disengagement was orderly.

phases.title: Orléans marches away with half of the third division
phases.text: As the Dauphin's division recoiled there was confusion in the French ranks. Orléans marched away with half of the third division, and the 1,600 who stayed launched a feeble attack that was repelled easily.
phases.quote: marched away from the battle with half of them

phases.title: Warwick's men pursue the French
phases.text: After the failed attack a number, possibly a large number, of men from Warwick's division left their positions and pursued the French, one motive being the ransom of prisoners.
phases.quote: a number, possibly a large number, of men from Warwick's division left their positions and pursued the French

phases.title: The King's division advances with the Oriflamme
phases.text: Survivors of the earlier attacks rallied to the King, and his division marched across the one-mile gap towards the exhausted Anglo-Gascons, all on foot. The Oriflamme was unfurled, the signal that no prisoners were to be taken.
phases.quote: The King ordered the French sacred banner, the Oriflamme, to be unfurled

phases.title: The Captal de Buch rides round the flank
phases.text: The Anglo-Gascon commanders thought they would be defeated if they stood to face a fourth attack. They sent a small mounted group under the Captal de Buch on a circuitous march round the French flank to strike the rear.
phases.quote: send a small mounted group under the Gascon lord Jean, the Captal de Buch, on a circuitous march around the French flank

phases.title: The Prince orders a general advance
phases.text: Concerned that his army would break, the Black Prince ordered a general advance, and the Anglo-Gascons moved forward out of their defensive positions. The French men-at-arms charged home into them.
phases.quote: Concerned his army would break and rout in the face of the French assault, the Black Prince gave the order for a general advance.

phases.title: Warwick's men return and steady the line
phases.text: The Anglo-Gascon line was starting to break when men of Warwick's division returned from their pursuit and reinforced it. This heartened the Anglo-Gascons and discouraged the French.
phases.quote: The Anglo-Gascon line was starting to break when it was reinforced by men of Warwick's division returning from their pursuit.

phases.title: The Captal's force arrives behind the French
phases.text: The Captal de Buch's 160 men arrived undetected in the French rear. His 100 archers dismounted and fired into it, and his 60 mounted men-at-arms charged into the back of the French line.
phases.quote: the Captal de Buch's 160 men arrived undetected in the French rear

phases.title: The French break and the King surrenders
phases.text: Some Frenchmen began to run, others copied them and the division fell apart. Those still fighting round the King were forced into a loop of the River Miosson and surrounded, and John and his youngest son surrendered.
phases.quote: The French still fighting around their King were forced into a loop of the River Miosson
